class MyLogger:
    """
    This class helps to suppress logs in lightgbm and Optuna
    Source - https://github.com/microsoft/LightGBM/issues/6014
    """

    def init(self, logging_lbl: str):
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(logging_lbl)
        self.logger.setLevel(logging.ERROR)

    def info(self, message):
        pass

    def warning(self, message):
        pass

    def error(self, message):
        self.logger.error(message)

class XGBLogging(xgb.callback.TrainingCallback):
    """log train logs to file"""

    def __init__(self, epoch_log_interval=100):
        self.epoch_log_interval = epoch_log_interval

    def after_iteration(self, model, epoch:int,
                        evals_log:xgb.callback.TrainingCallback.EvalsLog
                        ):

        if self.epoch_log_interval <= 0:
            pass

        elif (epoch %  self.epoch_log_interval == 0):
            for data, metric in evals_log.items():
                for metric_name, log in metric.items():
                    score = log[-1][0] if isinstance(log[-1], tuple) else log[-1]
                    logger.info(f"XGBLogging epoch {epoch} dataset {data} {metric_name} {score}")

        return False

class AdversarialCVMaker:
    """
    This class assists in adversarial CV between the train and test data with the below steps-

    1. Consider any classifier as a base model, I prefer any boosted tree model as I don't have to focus too much on preprocessing
    2. Load the train and test set features
    3. Make a new target column with 1 for test set occurrances and 0 for train-set
    4. Classify to predict the test set instances with the features and new target from the step above
    
    If the AUC score hovers around 50% (random model), then we can be sure that the train and test set have similar distributions 
    Else, if our model is able to differentiate between the train and test data, then our model is unlikely to generalize as-is.
    In this case, further adjustments may be necesary 
    """

    def __init__(self, n_splits: int = 5) :
        self.model = \
        LGBMC(
            n_estimators     = 200,
            learning_rate    = 0.02,
            max_depth        = 3, 
            colsample_bytree = 0.50,
            objective        = "binary",
            metric           = "auc",
            random_state     = 42,
            device           = "gpu" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu",
        )

        self.n_splits = n_splits

    @staticmethod
    def scorer(ytrue, ypreds):
        return roc_auc_score( ytrue, ypreds )

    def make_cv(
        self, Xtrain, Xtest, **fit_params,
        ):
        "Fits the model with the auxilary target and calculates the AUC score for the CV"

        df = \
        pd.concat(
            [Xtrain.assign(**{"target" : 0}), 
             Xtest.assign(**{"target" : 1}),
            ], 
            axis=0, ignore_index = True
        )

        cv     = StratifiedKFold(n_splits = self.n_splits, random_state = 42, shuffle = True)
        scores = 0
        
        for train_idx, dev_idx in cv.split(df, df["target"]) :
            Xtr  = df.loc[train_idx].drop("target", axis=1)
            Xdev = df.loc[dev_idx].drop("target", axis=1)
            ytr  = df.loc[train_idx, "target"]
            ydev = df.loc[dev_idx, "target"]

            cat_cols = list( Xdev.select_dtypes(include = ["string", "category", "object"]).columns )

            if len(cat_cols) > 0 :
                Xtr[cat_cols]  = Xtr[cat_cols].astype("category")
                Xdev[cat_cols] = Xdev[cat_cols].astype("category")
            else:
                pass
                
            model = clone(self.model)
            model.fit(Xtr, ytr)
            dev_preds = model.predict_proba(Xdev)[:,1]
            score = self.scorer(ydev, dev_preds)
            scores += score

        score = scores / self.n_splits

        PrintColor(
            f"\n---> Overall adversarial CV score = {score :,.4f}"
        )

        if score > 0.60 :
            PrintColor(
                f"---> Check for test-train distribution shift\n", color = Fore.RED
            )
        else:
            PrintColor(
                f"---> Train-test distributions are similar\n", color = Fore.GREEN
            )

        self.original            = self.original[self.train.columns]

        self.sub_fl = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(CFG.ip_path, "sample_submission.csv"))
        PrintColor(
            f"Data shapes - train-test-original | {self.train.shape} {self.test.shape} {self.original.shape}"
        )

    
    def _VisualizeDF(self):
        "This method visualizes the heads for the train, test and original data"
        
        PrintColor(f"\nTrain set head", color = Fore.CYAN)
        display(self.train.head(5).style.format(precision = 3))
        
        PrintColor(f"\nTest set head", color = Fore.CYAN)
        display(self.test.head(5).style.format(precision = 3))
        
        PrintColor(f"\nOriginal set head", color = Fore.CYAN)
        display(self.original.head(5).style.format(precision = 3))
              
    def _AddSourceCol(self):
        self.train['Source']    = "Competition"
        self.test['Source']     = "Competition"
        self.original['Source'] = 'Original'
        
        self.strt_ftre = self.test.columns
        return self
          
    def _CollateInfoDesc(self):
        if self.dtl_preproc_req :
            PrintColor(f"\n{'-' * 20} Information and description {'-' * 20}\n", color = Fore.MAGENTA);

            # Creating dataset information and description:
            for lbl, df in {'Train': self.train, 'Test': self.test, 'Original': self.original}.items():
                PrintColor(f"\n{lbl} description\n");
                display(df.describe(percentiles= [0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99]).\
                        transpose().\
                        drop(columns = ['count'], errors = 'ignore').\
                        drop([self.target], axis=0, errors = 'ignore').\
                        style.format(formatter = '{:,.2f}').\
                        background_gradient(cmap = 'Blues')
                       );

                PrintColor(f"\n{lbl} information\n");
                display(df.info());
                collect();
        return self;
    
    def _CollateUnqNull(self):
        
        if self.dtl_preproc_req :
            PrintColor(f"\nUnique and null values\n")
            _ = pd.concat([self.train[self.strt_ftre].nunique(), 
                           self.test[self.strt_ftre].nunique(), 
                           self.original[self.strt_ftre].nunique(),
                           self.train[self.strt_ftre].isna().sum(axis=0),
                           self.test[self.strt_ftre].isna().sum(axis=0),
                           self.original[self.strt_ftre].isna().sum(axis=0)
                          ], 
                          axis=1)
            _.columns = ['Train_Nunq', 'Test_Nunq', 'Original_Nunq', 
                         'Train_Nulls', 'Test_Nulls', 'Original_Nulls'
                        ]
            display(_.T.style.background_gradient(cmap = 'Blues', axis=1).\
                    format(formatter = '{:,.0f}')
                   )
            
        return self
       
    def _ConjoinTrainOrig(self):
        if self.conjoin_orig_data :
            PrintColor(f"\n\nTrain shape before conjoining with original = {self.train.shape}")
            train = pd.concat([self.train] + [self.original] * CFG.nb_orig, 
                              axis=0, 
                              ignore_index = True
                             )
            PrintColor(f"Train shape after conjoining with original= {train.shape}")

            train.index = range(len(train))
            train.index.name = 'id'

        else:
            PrintColor(f"\nWe are using the competition training data only")
            train = self.train
        return train
       
    def DoPreprocessing(self):
        self._VisualizeDF()
        self._AddSourceCol()
        self._CollateInfoDesc()
        self._CollateUnqNull()
        self.train = self._ConjoinTrainOrig()

        self.train = self.train.dropna(subset = [self.target])
        self.train.index = range(len(self.train))
        
        self.cat_cols  = \
        list(
            self.test.drop("Source", axis=1).select_dtypes(["object", "string", "category"]).columns
        )
        self.cont_cols = \
        [c for c in self.strt_ftre if c not in self.cat_cols + ['Source']]
        
        return self ;

def reindex_oof(oof_ids, oof_proba, n_train):
    """
    Place OOF probabilities into a full (n_train, n_classes) matrix
    using oof_ids as the row index mapping.

    Parameters
    ----------
    oof_ids : np.ndarray, shape (n_oof,)
        Row indices into the training set corresponding to each OOF row.
    oof_proba : np.ndarray, shape (n_oof, n_classes)
        OOF probabilities in the order produced by the base model.
    n_train : int
        Total number of training samples.

    Returns
    -------
    meta_X_train : np.ndarray, shape (n_train, n_classes)
        Probability matrix with rows placed at positions given by oof_ids.
        Rows not covered by oof_ids remain zero.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If oof_ids contains out-of-bound indices or oof_ids/oof_proba
        row counts do not match.
    """
    oof_ids   = np.asarray(oof_ids,   dtype=np.intp)
    oof_proba = np.asarray(oof_proba, dtype=np.float64)

    if oof_ids.shape[0] != oof_proba.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"oof_ids length {oof_ids.shape[0]} does not match "
            f"oof_proba row count {oof_proba.shape[0]}."
        )
    if oof_ids.max() >= n_train or oof_ids.min() < 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"oof_ids values must be in [0, n_train); "
            f"got range [{oof_ids.min()}, {oof_ids.max()}] with n_train={n_train}."
        )

    meta_X_train = np.zeros((n_train, oof_proba.shape[1]), dtype=np.float64)
    meta_X_train[oof_ids] = oof_proba
    return meta_X_train


from scipy.optimize import minimize

class TunedBlender:
    """
    A stacking meta-learner that blends base model OOF probability outputs
    using a log-transformed Logistic Regression with per-fold threshold tuning.

    Architecture
    ------------
    For each CV fold:
        1. Fit a Pipeline(log1p → LogisticRegression) on the training split of
           the stacked OOF probability matrix.
        2. Generate val-fold probabilities and tune per-class multiplicative
           weights on that fold via Nelder-Mead optimisation.
        3. Generate test-set probabilities from the fold model.
        4. Apply the fold-tuned weights to test probs → fold test labels.

    After all folds:
        - OOF probs are stitched from each val-fold's raw probabilities.
        - OOF labels are argmax(oof_probs * mean_weights).
        - Test probs are averaged across folds.
        - Final test labels are argmax(avg_test_probs * mean_weights).

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_splits : int, default=5
        Number of stratified CV folds.
    lr_kwargs : dict, optional
        Keyword arguments forwarded to LogisticRegression.
        Defaults to max_iter=1000, class_weight='balanced'.
    random_state : int, default=42
        Controls StratifiedKFold and LogisticRegression shuffling.

    Attributes
    ----------
    oof_probs_ : np.ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
        Raw val-fold probabilities stitched in original row order.
    oof_labels_ : np.ndarray, shape (n_samples,)
        argmax(oof_probs_ * mean_weights_) — tuned OOF class predictions.
    test_probs_ : np.ndarray, shape (n_test_samples, n_classes)
        Average of per-fold test probabilities.
    test_labels_ : np.ndarray, shape (n_test_samples,)
        argmax(test_probs_ * mean_weights_) — final test class predictions.
    fold_weights_ : list of np.ndarray
        Per-class multiplicative weights found by threshold optimisation in
        each fold.
    mean_weights_ : np.ndarray, shape (n_classes,)
        Element-wise mean of fold_weights_, applied for final label decoding.
    oof_score_ : float
        Balanced accuracy of oof_labels_ against the true training labels.
    """

    def __init__(self, n_splits=5, lr_kwargs=None, random_state=42):
        self.n_splits = n_splits
        self.random_state = random_state
        self.lr_kwargs = lr_kwargs or {
            "max_iter"     : 100000,
            "class_weight" : "balanced",
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def _to_numpy(x, name="input"):
        """
        Coerce x to a 2-D float64 numpy array.

        Accepts
        -------
        - np.ndarray  (1-D or 2-D)
        - pd.DataFrame
        - pd.Series   (treated as a single column)

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError  if the type is not supported.
        ValueError if the result is not 2-D after coercion.
        """
        if isinstance(x, pd.DataFrame):
            arr = x.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
        elif isinstance(x, pd.Series):
            arr = x.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, 1)
        elif isinstance(x, np.ndarray):
            arr = x.astype(np.float64, copy=False)
            if arr.ndim == 1:
                arr = arr.reshape(-1, 1)
        else:
            raise TypeError(
                f"{name} must be a pd.DataFrame, pd.Series, or np.ndarray; "
                f"got {type(x).__name__}."
            )
        if arr.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{name} must be 2-D after coercion; got shape {arr.shape}."
            )
        return arr

    def _make_pipeline(self):
        """Build a fresh log1p → LogisticRegression pipeline."""
        return Pipeline([
            ("log1p", FunctionTransformer(np.log1p, validate=True)),
            ("lr", LRC(
                random_state=self.random_state,
                **self.lr_kwargs
            )),
        ])

    @staticmethod
    def _tune_weights(probs, labels):
        """
        Find per-class multiplicative weights that maximise balanced accuracy
        on (probs, labels) via Nelder-Mead minimisation.

        Parameters
        ----------
        probs : np.ndarray, shape (n, n_classes)
        labels : np.ndarray, shape (n,)

        Returns
        -------
        best_weights : np.ndarray, shape (n_classes,)
        """
        n_classes = probs.shape[1]

        def objective(weights):
            preds = np.argmax(probs * weights, axis=1)
            return -balanced_accuracy_score(labels, preds)

        result = minimize(
            objective,
            x0=np.ones(n_classes),
            method="Nelder-Mead",
            options={"maxiter": 5000, "xatol": 1e-5, "fatol": 1e-5},
        )
        return result.x

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Fit-predict 
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def fit_predict(self, meta_X_train, meta_X_test, y_train):
        """
        Run CV blending with per-fold threshold tuning.

        Parameters
        ----------
        meta_X_train : np.ndarray or pd.DataFrame, shape (n_train, k)
            Stacked OOF probabilities from base models (training set).
        meta_X_test : np.ndarray or pd.DataFrame, shape (n_test, k)
            Stacked test probabilities from base models.
        y_train : array-like, shape (n_train,)
            True class labels for the training set.

        Returns
        -------
        oof_probs : np.ndarray, shape (n_train, n_classes)
        oof_labels : np.ndarray, shape (n_train,)
        test_probs : np.ndarray, shape (n_test, n_classes)
        test_labels : np.ndarray, shape (n_test,)
        """
        # ── Input coercion — accept DataFrame or ndarray for both matrices ──
        meta_X_train = self._to_numpy(meta_X_train, name="meta_X_train")
        meta_X_test  = self._to_numpy(meta_X_test,  name="meta_X_test")
        y_train      = np.asarray(y_train)

        skf = StratifiedKFold(
            n_splits=self.n_splits,
            shuffle=True,
            random_state=self.random_state,
        )

        n_train = meta_X_train.shape[0]

        # Placeholders — n_classes resolved on first fold
        oof_probs_buf  = None
        fold_test_probs = []    # (n_splits, n_test, n_classes)
        self.fold_weights_ = []

        for fold_idx, (tr_idx, val_idx) in enumerate(
            skf.split(meta_X_train, y_train)
        ):
            X_tr, X_val = meta_X_train[tr_idx], meta_X_train[val_idx]
            y_tr, y_val = y_train[tr_idx], y_train[val_idx]

            # ── 1. Fit pipeline on training split of this fold ──────────
            pipe = self._make_pipeline()
            pipe.fit(X_tr, y_tr)

            # ── 2. Val-fold probabilities & threshold optimisation ───────
            val_probs = pipe.predict_proba(X_val)   # (n_val, n_classes)

            if oof_probs_buf is None:
                n_classes = val_probs.shape[1]
                oof_probs_buf = np.zeros((n_train, n_classes))

            oof_probs_buf[val_idx] = val_probs

            fold_weights = self._tune_weights(val_probs, y_val)
            self.fold_weights_.append(fold_weights)

            # ── 3. Test probabilities from this fold model ───────────────
            test_probs_fold = pipe.predict_proba(meta_X_test)
            fold_test_probs.append(test_probs_fold)

        # ── Post-fold aggregation ────────────────────────────────────────
        self.mean_weights_ = np.mean(self.fold_weights_, axis=0)

        print("\nPer-fold Tuned Weights")
        for i, w in enumerate(self.fold_weights_):
            print(f"  Fold {i+1}: {np.array2string(w, precision = 5, separator=', ')}")
        print(f"  Mean : {np.array2string(self.mean_weights_, precision=5, separator=', ')}")

        # OOF
        self.oof_probs_  = oof_probs_buf
        self.oof_labels_ = np.argmax(
            self.oof_probs_ * self.mean_weights_, axis=1
        )
        self.oof_score_ = balanced_accuracy_score(y_train, self.oof_labels_)

        # Test
        self.test_probs_  = np.mean(fold_test_probs, axis=0)
        self.test_labels_ = np.argmax(
            self.test_probs_ * self.mean_weights_, axis=1
        )

        return (
            self.oof_probs_,
            self.oof_labels_,
            self.test_probs_,
            self.test_labels_,
        )
